correctness.rationale: For even \(q\), nonidentity centralizers are abelian and the nonidentity commuting graph is a disjoint union of cliques; adjoining the identity preserves chordality. The same holds for \(q=5\cong A_5\). For odd \(q>5\), the unique involution class has \(n=q(q+\chi)/2\) vertices, with \(\chi=1\) for \(q\equiv1\pmod4\) and \(-1\) otherwise, and degree \(k=(q-\chi)/2\ge4\). A commuting involution clique has size at most three because an involution centralizer is dihedral with elementary abelian two-subgroups of order at most four. Thus the induced involution graph has \(nk/2\ge2n\) edges, while every chordal graph with clique number at most three has at most \(2n-3\) edges. Hence the involution graph, and therefore the full commuting graph, is nonchordal. The bundled verifier checks the exact involution counts for prime fields \(5,7,11,13\), an induced six-cycle at \(q=7\), and the arithmetic inequality; the proof covers all prime powers, including \(q=9\).
